animal_cow_mastitis.title: Cow Mastitis
animal_cow_mastitis.overview: Mastitis is a bacterial infection of the udder causing swelling, clots in milk, fever, and reduced milk yield.
animal_cow_mastitis.treatment_organic: Wash udder with warm saline water 2–3 times daily. Apply turmeric + aloe vera paste externally. Use neem leaf warm compress for inflammation.
animal_cow_mastitis.treatment_chemical: Use intramammary antibiotics only as prescribed by a veterinarian. Anti-inflammatory injections may be required.
animal_cow_mastitis.prevention: Maintain clean housing, ensure proper milking hygiene, disinfect teats after milking, keep bedding dry.
animal_cow_mastitis.immediate_steps: Isolate the cow, stop using milk for consumption, call a vet immediately.

animal_goat_healthy.title: Goat Healthy
animal_goat_healthy.overview: No visible disease detected. The goat appears healthy based on the image.
animal_goat_healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced nutrition, provide clean drinking water, follow regular vaccination and deworming schedule.
animal_goat_healthy.immediate_steps: Continue regular care and monitor the goat for unusual symptoms.

animal_goat_ppr.title: Goat PPR (Peste des Petits Ruminants)
animal_goat_ppr.overview: PPR is a highly contagious viral disease found in goats, causing fever, nasal discharge, mouth ulcers, diarrhea, and pneumonia.
animal_goat_ppr.treatment_organic: Provide warm water, electrolytes, and herbal immunity boosters (giloy, tulsi). Maintain hydration and isolate the animal.
animal_goat_ppr.treatment_chemical: No direct cure; treatment is supportive. Broad-spectrum antibiotics may be given by a vet to prevent secondary infections.
animal_goat_ppr.prevention: Annual PPR vaccination, quarantine new animals for 15 days, disinfect housing regularly.
animal_goat_ppr.immediate_steps: Isolate the sick goat immediately, provide electrolytes, contact a veterinarian urgently.

plant_paddy_blast.title: Paddy Blast (Leaf Blast / Neck Blast)
plant_paddy_blast.overview: Blast disease is caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae. It creates diamond-shaped lesions and reduces yield drastically.
plant_paddy_blast.treatment_organic: Spray neem oil extract, panchagavya, or fermented buttermilk. Remove infected leaves and improve airflow.
plant_paddy_blast.treatment_chemical: Apply Tricyclazole, Carbendazim, or Propiconazole following agriculture department guidelines.
plant_paddy_blast.prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer, maintain proper field drainage.
plant_paddy_blast.immediate_steps: Spray fungicide immediately in affected patches and inform local agriculture extension officer.

plant_paddy_blight.title: Paddy Blight (Bacterial Leaf Blight)
plant_paddy_blight.overview: Bacterial blight in rice is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae leading to yellowing and wilting of leaves.
plant_paddy_blight.treatment_organic: Use cow urine extract foliar spray, apply fermented jaggery mixture, improve soil health.
plant_paddy_blight.treatment_chemical: Copper-based bactericides like Copper Oxychloride or Streptocycline may be used as per recommendations.
plant_paddy_blight.prevention: Use disease-free seeds, apply balanced nutrients, avoid water stagnation.
plant_paddy_blight.immediate_steps: Remove infected clumps, improve field drainage, and spray bactericide if recommended locally.

plant_paddy_brownspot.title: Paddy Brown Spot
plant_paddy_brownspot.overview: Brown Spot is caused by Bipolaris oryzae and appears as circular brown lesions, often due to nutrient deficiency.
plant_paddy_brownspot.treatment_organic: Apply neem cake, seaweed extract, or compost tea. Improve soil potassium levels organically.
plant_paddy_brownspot.treatment_chemical: Use Mancozeb or Carbendazim-based fungicides based on severity.
plant_paddy_brownspot.prevention: Use treated seeds, ensure good potassium fertilization, avoid drought stress.
plant_paddy_brownspot.immediate_steps: Apply recommended fungicide and improve soil nutrient balance immediately.

plant_paddy_tungro.title: Paddy Tungro Virus
plant_paddy_tungro.overview: Tungro is a viral disease spread by leafhoppers, causing orange-yellow discoloration, stunting, and reduced tillering.
plant_paddy_tungro.treatment_organic: Remove infected plants, use neem oil spray to suppress leafhopper activity.
plant_paddy_tungro.treatment_chemical: Apply insecticides like Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam, or recommended alternatives for vector control.
plant_paddy_tungro.prevention: Use resistant varieties, synchronize planting, and control weeds that host leafhoppers.
plant_paddy_tungro.immediate_steps: Rogue out (remove) infected plants immediately and spray insecticide to control leafhoppers.
